thread:
carmen: Heads up — after the AWQ+FP8 kernel routing rollout yesterday we started seeing a spike of GPU OOMs on dedicated nodes serving 8k sequences. stack traces point at KV cache dtype casts and a sudden workspace growth. anyone else seeing this?

benp: saw two OOM alerts in the morning. p95 latency also up. attaching quick profiler snapshot below. not sure if it's kernel selection or allocator churn.

benp: ```
profiler_summary:
  peak_alloc: 12.4GB
  kv_cache: 4.8GB (stored as fp32 before cast)
  transient_buffers: 5.2GB
  workspace: 2.3GB
  alloc_ops/sec: 1150
  free_ops/sec: 1128
```

maya: looks like we're double-buffering during kv cast path. AWQ path tries FP8 kernels but we still keep kv in fp32 for correctness, then cast on request which triggers extra allocs.

arjun: my guess is allocator fragmentation + small transient allocations for cast buffers. buddy allocator tuning might help but we should try reuse. can you dump the alloc map?

benp: ran `rdw-prof --pid 2145 --alloc-map | jq '.slabs | length'` — got ~240 slabs on a 24GB GPU, heavy fragmentation.

priya: metrics show throughput -12% and p95 latency +30% for routes hitting prefer_fp8 kernels since the rollout. this lines up with extra memory churn.

oom-watcher-bot: Detected 3 OOM events on dedicated-3 between 2025-11-02T07:12 and 2025-11-02T08:03, reasons: temporary allocation spike during KV dtype cast.

carmen: temporary mitigation: revert kernel_policy to `safe` for AWQ models on dedicated pool, enable buffer_reuse and enforce kv_cache dtype=fp16. small canary first.

deploy-bot: rolled back kernel-routing v2 -> v1 on group=dedicated-3 (deploy id: dpl-20251102-0783) :white_check_mark:

arjun: proposed allocator tweaks for a canary: reduce `min_slab` to 512KB, increase `reuse_threshold` to 24h, enable slab compaction heuristics when fragmentation > 20%. also enable `workspace_reuse: true`. should cut transient allocs.

maya: also propose changing kv path to store primary as fp16 when model quant profile allows it. AWQ models we onboarded accept fp16 kv in 99% of cases; keep fp32 as fallback via flag `kv_keep_fp32=false` for canary.

benp: quick test config I'm going to try on canary: ```yaml
experiment: awq-rollback-canary
nodes: dedicated-3-canary
router:
  kernel_policy: safe
  batch_max_tokens: 4096
  prefer_fp8: true
  kv_dtype_policy: prefer_fp16
allocator:
  min_slab_bytes: 524288
  reuse_threshold_secs: 86400
  compact_frag_threshold_pct: 20
runtime:
  workspace_reuse: true
  kv_fallback_fp32: true
```

priya: sounds good. add tracing hooks to capture per-request alloc timeline so we can correlate with latency spikes.

arjun: I'll run an allocator sweep and produce flamegraphs for alloc/free.

maya: I'll re-run AWQ profiling with `--kv-store=fp16` and post diffs.

benp: I'll prepare perf regression dashboard comparing before/after for p50/p95/p99 and memory RSS.

carmen: thanks — plan: canary deploy in 30m, monitor OOMs/latency for 1h, then either promote or try stronger compaction. assign: @arjun allocator sweep, @maya AWQ profile, @benp dashboards.

priya: ack.

benp: one more note — mixed precision pitfalls: some kernels (nvptx optimized) require aligned strides; fp8 kernels sometimes allocate alignment padding which increases transient mem by ~5-8%. account for that in workspace sizing.

carmen: good catch. include `alignment_pad=4096` in canary allocator config.

arjun: got it. starting runs now. will post results here.

oom-watcher-bot: Canary started on dedicated-3-canary. monitor link: https://console/redwood/inference/canaries/awq-rollback-canary

carmen: great — keep updates short. thanks everyone.
